paper: Intra-Session recurrence in intradialytic hypotension prediction: evaluation implications and recurrence-aware modeling
authors_short: Kim S, Ryu J, Kim S, et al.
problem: Real-time intradialytic hypotension (IDH) prediction treats initial and recurrent IDH within a session as one class
method: ConvMixer/TCN/LSTM-attention vs rule-based naive baseline using only prior occurrence; recurrence-aware features + loss weighting; adversarial training across SBP subgroups
claimed_novelty: IDH probability rises from 0.7-10.4% before the initial event to 11.7-65.7% after it; pooled evaluation overestimates performance (big F1/AUPRC gap initial vs recurrent); a no-training prior-occurrence baseline reaches AUROC 0.798; recommends recurrence-stratified evaluation
what_they_do_not_do: Not ICU/OR; recurrence defined within a dialysis session (>=30 min after first IDH); AUROC/F1/AUPRC rather than alarm burden; no current-MAP comparator per stratum; no separate alarm budget per stratum; recurrence-aware modelling targets recurrent events, not the new-onset stratum
how_ours_differs: Same core phenomenon (C1, part of C2) shown in dialysis. Ours: continuous ICU/OR monitoring, 6-h look-back definition, event-level sensitivity at fixed alarms/patient-hour, shows the trained model is WORSE than current MAP on new-onset episodes in 3 cohorts, and a stratum-specific budget policy (C3) with an honest OR negative result. Must be cited as the closest prior work.

paper: Forecasting Seizures in Dogs with Naturally Occurring Epilepsy
authors_short: Howbert JJ, Patterson EE, Stead SM, et al.
problem: Seizure forecasting from continuous intracranial EEG
method: Logistic regression on iEEG band power; performance vs Poisson chance predictor with equal time-in-warning
claimed_novelty: Seizure clusters present in all dogs; restricting to 'lead seizures' (>=4 h after any previous seizure) reduces forecasting performance (significant in 2 of 3 dogs only)
what_they_do_not_do: Different organ/task; tiny sample; no model-vs-persistence baseline comparison per stratum; no stratified alarm budgets
how_ours_differs: Direct conceptual precedent for separating 'lead' (new-onset) from clustered (recurrent) events and for showing that pooled evaluation flatters forecasting. Ours transfers this to hypotension, quantifies it at fixed alarm burden, and adds the stratum-budget policy.

paper: Crowdsourcing reproducible seizure forecasting in human and canine epilepsy
authors_short: Brinkmann BH, Wagenaar J, Abbot D, et al.
problem: Reproducible benchmarking of seizure forecasting algorithms (Kaggle competition)
method: Crowdsourced classifiers of preictal vs interictal 10-min iEEG clips
data: Intracranial EEG from 5 dogs and 2 humans
claimed_novelty: Preictal clips drawn only from lead seizures (no seizure in the preceding 4 h) so clustered seizures do not drive the task
what_they_do_not_do: Uses lead-only definition by design; does not compare lead vs clustered performance; clip-level AUC, not alarm burden
how_ours_differs: Shows the 'new-onset only' target definition is standard in seizure forecasting; ours shows why it matters for hypotension and evaluates both strata with a shared alarm budget.

paper: Online Prediction of Lead Seizures from iEEG Data
authors_short: Chen H-H, Shiao H-T, Cherkassky V
problem: Online prediction of lead seizures from long-term iEEG
method: Group-learning SVM with periodic retraining and adaptive post-processing; reports sensitivity, time-in-warning, false positives/day
claimed_novelty: Targets lead seizures only because strong clustering yields few lead seizures (~7/dog), making prediction harder
what_they_do_not_do: Not hypotension; no comparison against a recurrence/persistence baseline; no recurrent stratum
how_ours_differs: Analogous new-onset-only target with alarm-burden style metrics; ours evaluates both strata and a state-aware budget split.

paper: Methodologic Insights on Building and Evaluating Models for Early Warning of Hypotension during Surgery
authors_short: Aubouin-Pairault B, Moussa K, Alamir M, et al.
problem: How data selection affects the measured performance of intraoperative hypotension early-warning models
method: Forward framing; train/test with or without segments with ongoing hypotension or classification-altering interventions; AUPRC, AUC and a clinician-oriented metric
claimed_novelty: Including ongoing hypotension at prediction time in evaluation inflates AUPRC by 72%; recommends testing without ongoing hypotension and without classification-altering interventions
what_they_do_not_do: Excludes only ONGOING hypotension, not recent (hours-earlier) hypotension; no new-onset vs recurrent split; no fixed alarm-burden comparison against current MAP per stratum; OR only
how_ours_differs: Closest perioperative precedent for C1 (evaluation contaminated by hypotensive state). Ours goes one step further: even after excluding ongoing hypotension, recent episodes (prior 6 h) dominate and drive the model's advantage; we test ICU and OR.

paper: The dynamics of arterial pressure itself predict intraoperative hypotension beyond its current value: an interpretable additive model validated in 3,069 external patients under a selection-bias-resistant protocol
authors_short: Oyarzun R, Hernández-Hernández P
problem: Whether IOH predictors add information beyond current MAP under bias-resistant evaluation
method: Additive GBM on current MAP, drift from 20-min baseline and rolling-variance growth; MAP-only comparator; grey-zone and already-hypotensive samples excluded; pre-registered external validation
data: VitalDB (807 patients) development; MOVER (3,069 patients) external
claimed_novelty: Small but consistent AUROC gain over MAP alone (+0.02-0.06) under strict protocol
what_they_do_not_do: No split by prior hypotension; AUROC not alarm burden; ICU not studied
how_ours_differs: Same 'beat current MAP' framing; ours shows the trained model's margin over MAP vanishes/reverses specifically on new-onset episodes.

paper: Blood pressure history improves near-term hypotension prediction and reassessment prioritisation in sepsis
authors_short: Wang L, Zhu J, Zhou R, et al.
problem: Predicting recurrent hypotension within 4 h in sepsis after target pressure is reached
method: GBM with 24 pressure-history predictors, patient-level cross-fitting; chronological replay with prompt counts; target-trial emulation
claimed_novelty: Pressure history raises AUROC over current information (0.840 vs 0.791 MIMIC-IV) and captures more episodes at equal prompt counts
what_they_do_not_do: Treats prior pressure history as useful signal; does not separate first vs recurrent episodes in evaluation; does not ask whether the gain is confined to recurrent episodes
how_ours_differs: Opposite emphasis: they exploit history to predict recurrence; we show history-driven gains do not carry over to new-onset episodes and allocate budget accordingly. Useful foil.

paper: Compact clinical features capturing organ history for dynamic prediction of organ deterioration in sepsis
authors_short: Wang L, Song J, Vereshchako M, et al.
problem: 6-h organ deterioration among organs with low recorded severity in sepsis
method: Large feature model reduced to 175 variables; compares 12 historical sources; alert policy with >=4 h between alerts and 0.5 alerts/patient
claimed_novelty: Historical features increase event capture at a fixed alert budget (+30% in eICU)
what_they_do_not_do: Focuses on low-severity organs but does not contrast new-onset vs recurrent deterioration or check a current-value baseline per stratum
how_ours_differs: Shows fixed-alert-budget evaluation and history features in ICU; ours shows the stratum where history cannot help (new-onset) and budgets it separately.

paper: Hypotension in ICU Patients Receiving Vasopressor Therapy
authors_short: Yapps B, Shin S, Bighamian R, et al.
problem: BP-goal compliance and advance warning of hypotension during vasopressor infusion
method: Logistic regression on BP-trend features vs simple threshold alert; advance forecast time
claimed_novelty: Hypotension episodes are frequent and recurrent (102/215 stays had >1 episode, median 2.5/day); trend model gives ~12-22 min lead time vs 0 for threshold
what_they_do_not_do: No new-onset vs recurrent stratification; no alarm-burden matched comparison
how_ours_differs: Documents that ICU hypotension is highly recurrent (supports C1 premise); ours quantifies how that recurrence dominates evaluation.

paper: The Value of Short-term Physiological History and Contextual Data in Predicting Hypotension in the ICU Settings
authors_short: Moghadam MC, Masoumi E, Kendale SM, Bagherzadeh N
venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine Update
problem: ICU hypotension prediction up to 30 min ahead from 5 min of physiology plus context
method: ML classifier with demographics, pre-ICU meds, comorbidities, physiological features
data: ICU data (UNVERIFIED: dataset not stated in abstract)
claimed_novelty: Contextual data add nothing; MAP-to-HR ratio and RR interval most important
what_they_do_not_do: No analysis of prior hypotension as predictor; no new-onset stratum; no alarm burden
how_ours_differs: Peripheral: history/context features; ours isolates recent-hypotension state as the source of apparent skill.

paper: Intraoperative Hypotension Prediction: Current Methods, Controversies, and Research Outlook
authors_short: Mukkamala R, Schnetz MP, Khanna AK, Mahajan A
problem: Review of IOH prediction methods and controversies
method: Narrative review with recommendations on event definitions and evaluation
claimed_novelty: Most methods rely heavily on prevailing MAP; good sensitivity/specificity but low PPV; calls for better event definitions and evaluation
what_they_do_not_do: No empirical new-onset vs recurrent analysis
how_ours_differs: Frames the MAP-dependence controversy that our C2 extends with a state-stratified, alarm-burden analysis.

paper: CON: The hypotension prediction index is not a validated predictor of hypotension
authors_short: Vistisen ST, Enevoldsen J
problem: Validity of the Hypotension Prediction Index
method: Position paper
claimed_novelty: Selection bias may have forced HPI to learn almost exclusively from MAP; HPI must show added value over a 70-75 mmHg MAP alarm
what_they_do_not_do: Concerns MAP shortcut via case selection, not recurrence; no stratification by prior hypotension
how_ours_differs: Ours identifies a second, distinct shortcut (recent-hypotension state) that persists even under unbiased every-time-point sampling.

paper: Evaluation of Sepsis Prediction Models before Onset of Treatment
authors_short: Kamran F, Tjandra D, Heiler A, et al.
problem: Do sepsis model predictions carry signal before clinicians recognise sepsis?
method: Evaluates Epic Sepsis Model AUROC restricted to predictions before treatment indicators (antibiotics, fluids, cultures, lactate)
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.62 overall falls to 0.47 when predictions after clinical recognition are excluded
what_they_do_not_do: Shortcut is clinician-recognition, not prior events; sepsis not hypotension; no alarm-budget policy
how_ours_differs: Strongest general precedent for C2's logic: apparent skill comes from patients whose state is already known. Ours shows the analogous effect for prior-hypotension state with a physiological (current MAP) baseline.

paper: External Validation of a Widely Implemented Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model in Hospitalized Patients
authors_short: Wong A, Otles E, Donnelly JP, et al.
problem: External validation of the Epic Sepsis Model
method: Hospitalisation-level and horizon AUROC; added benefit over usual care (timely antibiotics); alert burden
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.63; flagged only 183/2552 (7%) septic patients not already treated in time, while alerting on 18% of all patients
what_they_do_not_do: No recurrent-event analysis; shortcut framed as overlap with usual care
how_ours_differs: Precedent for measuring added value 'beyond what is already known'; ours does this per hypotension state at matched alarm burden.

paper: Machine learning for patient risk stratification: standing on, or looking over, the shoulders of clinicians?
authors_short: Beaulieu-Jones BK, Yuan W, Brat GA, et al.
problem: Whether EHR models learn patient physiology or clinician behaviour
method: Deep models trained on clinician-initiated/administrative data only
claimed_novelty: Clinician-action-only models approach full-EMR benchmarks; signal comes from 'looking over clinicians' shoulders'
what_they_do_not_do: Not time-series early warning; no prior-event stratification
how_ours_differs: General shortcut precedent; ours is a physiological-state shortcut in continuous monitoring.

paper: A framework for understanding label leakage in machine learning for health care
authors_short: Davis SE, Matheny ME, Balu S, Sendak MP
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
problem: When features carrying outcome information constitute harmful label leakage
method: Conceptual framework (cadence, perspective, applicability) with real-world examples
claimed_novelty: Leakage requires more nuance than the 'no time machine' rule
what_they_do_not_do: Not empirical; no recurrence analysis
how_ours_differs: Our recent-hypotension effect is not leakage in the strict sense (information is legitimately available) but a usefulness problem; the framework helps position C2.

paper: When Clinical Judgment Becomes a Predictive Shortcut: Two Questions Clinical AI Must Answer Before Deployment
authors_short: Yang J, Jiao LR, Zhang Z, Cai X
problem: Evidence requirements when clinical AI performance may derive from existing clinical judgment
method: Conceptual framework with state-reference and proxy-relative timing tests
claimed_novelty: Leakage checks, overall performance and external validation do not establish usefulness before recognition
what_they_do_not_do: No empirical hypotension work; no recurrence stratification
how_ours_differs: Ours supplies an empirical 'state-reference' test (new-onset stratum) for hypotension warnings.

paper: The Impact of Evaluation Strategy on Sepsis Prediction Model Performance Metrics in Intensive Care Data: Retrospective Cohort Study
authors_short: Do D-K, Rockenschaub P, Boie SD, et al.
problem: How evaluation strategy changes sepsis-model metrics
method: Fixed-horizon vs peak-score vs continuous evaluation of a MIMIC-IV-trained TCN applied to BerlinICU
claimed_novelty: Same model/data give markedly different metrics across strategies; continuous evaluation recommended
what_they_do_not_do: No stratification by prior events; no alarm-budget policy
how_ours_differs: Ours adds another evaluation axis (event state) that changes conclusions even under continuous evaluation.

paper: Dynamic Survival Analysis for Early Event Prediction
authors_short: Yèche H, Burger M, Veshchezerova D, Rätsch G
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (CHIL) / arXiv
problem: Early event prediction with event-level alarm metrics in ICU
method: Dynamic survival models with risk localisation used for alarm prioritisation
data: ICU early-event-prediction benchmarks (UNVERIFIED: datasets not stated in abstract)
claimed_novelty: Alarm prioritisation improves event-level AuPRC by up to 11%
what_they_do_not_do: Single alarm policy across patients; no state-stratified budgets; no new-onset analysis
how_ours_differs: Shares the event-level/alarm-policy view; ours splits the budget by recent-hypotension state.

paper: Equality of Opportunity in Supervised Learning
authors_short: Hardt M, Price E, Srebro N
problem: Fair classification via post-processing
method: Group-specific decision thresholds chosen to equalise true-positive rates
claimed_novelty: Group-specific thresholds on an existing score can enforce equal opportunity
what_they_do_not_do: Groups are protected attributes, not clinical states; no time series or alarm budgets
how_ours_differs: Methodological ancestor of C3 (separate thresholds per stratum under a shared constraint); our strata are dynamic clinical states and the constraint is total alarms/patient-hour.

paper: Staffable ICU early-warning with calibrated multi-centre validation and alert-budget guardrails
authors_short: Zafar SA, Qin W, Soomro TA, et al.
problem: Workload-constrained ICU early-warning thresholds
method: Multi-horizon mortality model; thresholds translated to alerts/100 admissions and clinician time; guardrails
claimed_novelty: Alert-budget guardrails bound workload while preserving utility
what_they_do_not_do: Single global threshold per horizon; mortality not hypotension; no state-specific budgets
how_ours_differs: Alarm budget as design constraint is shared; ours allocates the budget across hypotension states.

paper: Artificial Intelligence-powered tiered early warning framework addressing high false alarm rates for in-hospital mortality prediction
authors_short: Wu L, Mai L, Wang H, et al.
problem: False alarms in ED mortality prediction
method: Two-stage tiered thresholds + LLM/SHAP filtering
claimed_novelty: Tiered thresholds raise PPV from 10-19% to 33-41%
what_they_do_not_do: Risk tiers on one score, not separate models/budgets for clinical states; not continuous monitoring
how_ours_differs: Tiered thresholding precedent; ours uses state-specific models and budgets under fixed total burden.

paper: Interpretable machine learning model for new-onset atrial fibrillation prediction in critically ill patients: a multi-center study
authors_short: Guan C, Gong A, Zhao Y, et al.
problem: New-onset AF prediction in ICU
method: LASSO + XGBoost with SHAP
claimed_novelty: Patient-level NOAF prediction (AUC 0.89 internal, 0.77 external)
what_they_do_not_do: Static patient-level 'new-onset' (vs pre-existing AF), not time-varying episode state; no recurrent comparison
how_ours_differs: Shows 'new-onset' framing is common for arrhythmia at patient level; ours defines new-onset dynamically (6-h look-back) and compares strata.
